basic angling licence

Not needed if you are a status First Nations person living in B.C.
To fish for steelhead

Anglers 16 and over need a Steelhead Conservation Surcharge Stamp to fish for steelhead on streams (not on a Classified Water whose row says “Steelhead Stamp not required”, while it is in force). This water
Steelhead Conservation Surcharge Stamp
To fish for white sturgeon
Anglers 16 and over need a White Sturgeon Conservation Licence to fish for white sturgeon. This water

To keep salmon

Conservation Surcharge Stamp for salmon
When you keep a fish you must record

Anglers 16 and over: carry your paper licence when keeping a fish whose retention you must record on your licence: hatchery steelhead, adult chinook, rainbow trout over 50 cm (Main body of Kootenay Lake), lake trout and Dolly Varden/bull trout over 60 cm (Shuswap Lake) or rainbow trout over 50 cm (Shuswap system). pos:vedder_515|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:vedder_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:klwa_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 2 trout and char a day you may have 4: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:klwa_1012|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 2 trout and char a day you may have 4: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:cow1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:cow2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:chw1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:chw2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:klmb_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:kluwa_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 2 trout and char a day you may have 4: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:wilkes_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:anderson_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 4 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.28 ↗

pos:bc1_501|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:bc0_501|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:bc1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:bc0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

Any fish snagged — even by accident — must be released.
When you release a fish
Gently, back in the water
Without harming it
When you keep a fish
It stays kept: no swapping for a bigger one
Don’t waste it
Don’t hold it alive (no stringer or livewell)
Leave head, tail and fins on until home
No canning or filleting until home
Don’t freeze fish into one block: each must stay countable
Each fish must stay identifiable and measurable
Carrying fish
Never more than your legal limit
Licence at hand while you travel with fish
Carrying someone else’s fish? Have their signed letter
Taking fish out of B.C.? Show the letter if asked
Given fish? Keep the signed letter until eaten
Never
Sell, buy or trade your catch
Keep or move live fish or crayfish
Release aquarium fish
Put gear in the water during a closure
Interfere with a fur trap
Cross private, posted or reserve land without permission

pos:ape_501|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:ape_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:glenn_501|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:glenn_615|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:glenn_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.

pos:hamill_615|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:hamill_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:iron_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x2p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 8 bass a day you may have 16: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.68 ↗

pos:x3p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 5 whitefish a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 3 Arctic grayling a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x4p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.28 ↗

pos:x5p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x9p6_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x9p4_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x9p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x9p8_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x9p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x9p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x9p5_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x12p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 whitefish a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x13p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x13p4_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x14p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x14p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x14p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x15p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x15p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x15p8_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.28 ↗

Any fish snagged — even by accident — must be released.

Gently, back in the water
Without harming it

Leave head, tail and fins on until home

Licence at hand while you travel with fish

Taking fish out of B.C.? Show the letter if asked
Given fish? Keep the signed letter until eaten

pos:x15p5_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x15p13_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.28 ↗

lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.

With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x15p15_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x15p6_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x15p16_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x15p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x15p17_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x15p18_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.58 ↗

pos:x15p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.58 ↗

pos:x16p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x16p8_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x16p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x16p4_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x16p6_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x16p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x16p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.13 ↗

pos:x17p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x17p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x17p4_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x17p7_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.

In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

Any fish snagged — even by accident — must be released.
When you release a fish
Gently, back in the water
Without harming it
When you keep a fish
It stays kept: no swapping for a bigger one
Don’t waste it
Don’t hold it alive (no stringer or livewell)
Leave head, tail and fins on until home
No canning or filleting until home
Don’t freeze fish into one block: each must stay countable
Each fish must stay identifiable and measurable
Carrying fish
Never more than your legal limit
Licence at hand while you travel with fish
Carrying someone else’s fish? Have their signed letter
Taking fish out of B.C.? Show the letter if asked
Given fish? Keep the signed letter until eaten
Never
Sell, buy or trade your catch
Keep or move live fish or crayfish
Release aquarium fish
Put gear in the water during a closure
Interfere with a fur trap
Cross private, posted or reserve land without permission

pos:x17p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x18p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x18p4_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x18p5_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x18p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x18p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x18p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 2 trout and char a day you may have 4: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 kokanee a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x19p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x19p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x19p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x19p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x19p6_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

groups.head: When you keep a fish

Given fish? Keep the signed letter until eaten

Interfere with a fur trap

pos:x19p7_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x19p4_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x20p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 4 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.28 ↗

lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 1 trout and char a day you may have 2: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x21p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x21p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.

With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x22p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Arctic grayling. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 3 walleye a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
With 3 northern pike a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.64 ↗

pos:x22p3_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Arctic grayling. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 3 walleye a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
With 3 northern pike a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.64 ↗

pos:x22p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Arctic grayling. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 3 walleye a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
With 3 northern pike a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.64 ↗

pos:x22p6_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Arctic grayling. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 2 Arctic grayling a day you may have 2: 1 day’s fish.
With 3 walleye a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
With 3 northern pike a day you may have 6: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.64 ↗

pos:x23p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x25p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish.
With 6 rainbow trout and steelhead a day you may have 12: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x26p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x27p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for Dolly Varden or bull trout. Fish at home don’t count. Possession: the daily quota for lake trout. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.

pos:x27p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.49 ↗

pos:x27p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.42 ↗

pos:x32p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 5 trout and char a day you may have 10: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 5 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.34 ↗

pos:x34p_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x37p1_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x37p2_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

pos:x37p0_1010|pos.title: Possession
lines: Possession: 2 days’ quota. Fish at home don’t count.
The fish you have with you at any time — in camp, a cooler or a vehicle.
For example:
With 4 trout and char a day you may have 8: 2 days’ fish. Possession doubles the 4 a day, not the 2 from streams.
With 15 whitefish a day you may have 30: 2 days’ fish.
With 20 bass a day you may have 40: 2 days’ fish.
In the rule book’s words

possession quota: the number of fish of any species that an angler may have in their possession at any given time, EXCEPT at place of ordinary residence. In most instances, the possession quota is two times the daily quota. See Tables for exceptions.
Source › Rule book p.21 ↗

gl:bait_ban.title: Bait ban
lines: No natural bait of any kind — worms, roe, insects, fish parts — for any fish, while the ban runs. Lures and flies are fine.
In the book’s words

Bait Ban: the use of natural bait is prohibited in waters with a bait ban. Bait may be banned year round or seasonally. During the period when bait is banned it is banned for all angling and for all species.
Rule book p.4 ↗ p.8 ↗

gl:conservation_surcharge.title: Conservation Surcharge Stamp
lines: An add-on to your basic licence that pays for conservation; you need one only for what it names: Kootenay Lake rainbow trout, Shuswap Lake char, Shuswap rainbow trout, salmon, Steelhead. Keeping some of these fish also means recording them on your licence right away.
In the book’s words
Your basic angling licence can be validated with up to five annual Conservation Surcharge Stamps, plus a White Sturgeon Conservation Licence.
Rule book p.5 ↗ p.7 ↗

gl:fly_fishing.title: Fly fishing only
lines: Only an artificial fly on the line (one single-pointed hook) — no bait or lure, no float or strike indicator, no sinker or split shot, no spinner or other attracting device. Where a water is fly fishing only, that is the only way to fish it.
In the book’s words

fly fishing: angling with a line to which only an artificial fly is attached (floats, sinkers, or attracting devices may not be attached to the line when fishing is restricted to "fly fishing only"). artificial fly: a single-pointed hook that is dressed only with fur, feathers, hair, textiles, tinsel and/or wire, and to which no external weight or external attracting device is attached. Two or more hooks tied in tandem is not permitted. Where gear is restricted to artificial flies, floats and sinkers may be attached to the line. Where areas are restricted to "fly fish only" floats and sinkers may not be attached to the line or fly.
Rule book p.80 ↗

gl:single_barbless_hook.title: Single barbless hook
lines: A hook with one point (no treble) and no barb — you may pinch the barb flat. Every river, stream, creek and slough in B.C. requires it; on a lake only where its row says so.
In the book’s words

barbless hook: a hook without a barb on any part of the hook, including both the point and shank. Existing tackle may be modified by completely removing the barb, or by crimping the barb down so that its point is flush against the shaft. single hook: a hook having only one point. (In contrast, a treble hook is a hook having three points on a common shaft.) Note: use of a treble hook is permitted unless "single hook" is specified. It is unlawful to use barbed hooks or a hook with more than one point in any river, stream, creek or slough in B.C. (Note: the use of barbed hooks in lakes is permitted, unless noted in the Regional Water-Specific Tables).
Rule book p.8 ↗ p.80 ↗

gl:steelhead.title: Steelhead
lines: A rainbow trout that went to sea and came back: on waters where they run, any rainbow over 50 cm is a steelhead and follows the steelhead rules. Every wild steelhead must be released; you may keep at most 10 hatchery steelhead a licence year in all of B.C.
In the book’s words

steelhead: a rainbow trout longer than 50 cm in waters where anadromous rainbow trout are found. Both hatchery and wild steelhead may be found in B.C. waters. The annual province-wide quota for hatchery steelhead is 10. All wild steelhead must be released. Your basic licence must be validated with a Conservation Surcharge Stamp if you fish for steelhead anywhere in B.C. (whether you keep or release your catch). You must immediately record your retention of hatchery steelhead on your basic angling licence.
Rule book p.6 ↗ p.80 ↗

gl:steelhead_stamp.title: Steelhead Stamp
lines: A Steelhead Conservation Surcharge Stamp, added to your basic licence. You need it to fish for steelhead anywhere in B.C., even if you release them — and on many Classified Waters, on set dates, whatever you fish for. $28.57 a year for B.C. residents, $68.57 for everyone else.
In the book’s words

The annual province-wide quota for hatchery steelhead is 10. All wild steelhead must be released. Your basic licence must be validated with a Conservation Surcharge Stamp if you fish for steelhead anywhere in B.C. (whether you keep or release your catch). You must immediately record your retention of hatchery steelhead on your basic angling licence.
Rule book p.5 ↗ p.6 ↗ p.7 ↗

gl:under_16.title: Anglers under 16
lines: B.C. residents under 16 need no licence or stamp and have their own quota. Under-16s from elsewhere need no licence either, but must fish with someone 16 or older who holds the licences and stamps the fishing needs — and what they keep counts toward that person's quota. To have their own quota, they buy the licences a 16+ angler would.
In the book’s words

If you are under 16 and NOT a resident of B.C.: You do not require any licence or stamp, but you must be accompanied by a person 16 years or older who holds the appropriate licences and stamps. Any fish you keep must be counted as part of the catch and possession of your accompanying licence holder.
Rule book p.6 ↗

hatch.title: Hatchery or wild?
lines: Wild · adipose fin there
Hatchery · clipped, a healed scar instead
Look on the back, just in front of the tail. A small fin there means wild. Only a scar means hatchery. If you can’t tell, treat the fish as wild.
Hatchery or wild (adipose fin)

Hatchery trout and steelhead are marked before release by removing the adipose fin — the small fleshy fin on the back between the dorsal fin and the tail — so a hatchery fish has a healed scar there. A fish with its adipose fin (or a fresh, unhealed wound) is wild. Where only hatchery fish may be kept, every wild one goes back.
In the book’s words

hatchery trout: in some waters, hatchery trout may be harvested but wild trout must be released. In these waters, hatchery trout are marked before stocking by removal of their adipose fin. Therefore, these hatchery trout must have a healed scar in place of the missing fin. wild trout: in some waters, hatchery trout may be harvested but wild trout must be released. In these waters, wild trout will not be marked as hatchery fish and will have a normal adipose fin, or will have an unhealed scar in place of that fin, if missing.
Rule book p.13 ↗ p.80 ↗

gl:classified_waters.title: Classified Waters (Class I, Class II)
lines: Highly productive trout streams listed in the tables as Class I or Class II (8 and 66 designations). While a water is classified you need a Classified Waters Licence on top of your basic licence: B.C. residents buy one a year ($17.15) for every classified water; anyone else buys it per day and per water ($45.72 Class I, $22.86 Class II).
In the book’s words

All anglers required to buy a basic angling licence must also purchase a Classified Waters Licence before fishing on a stream during the period when it is classified. This licence is required in addition to the basic angling licence and any other stamps required by regulation. Also note that a Steelhead Conservation Surcharge Stamp is required at all times when fishing for steelhead, or when fishing classified waters during the period when steelhead are known to be present. gl:artificial_fly.title: Artificial fly
lines: A single-pointed hook dressed only with fur, feathers, hair, textiles, tinsel or wire, with no weight or attractor of its own. Where flies only are allowed, no lure or bait hook — but a float or sinker may still be on the line.
In the book’s words

artificial fly: a single-pointed hook that is dressed only with fur, feathers, hair, textiles, tinsel and/or wire, and to which no external weight or external attracting device is attached. Two or more hooks tied in tandem is not permitted. Where gear is restricted to artificial flies, floats and sinkers may be attached to the line. Where areas are restricted to "fly fish only" floats and sinkers may not be attached to the line or fly.
